page.layout: One column of running text in roman type, with German glosses set in the same column. Running head "LATINA." and page number "51" at the top. Gathering signature "d 2" at the foot. No margin notes.

main_text.p: und klein. Abyssus,ein abgrund. Astragalus,ein würf-felspiel. Costus,ein kraut/ das eine wolriechige wur-zel hatt. Balanus,ein eychel/ein kapfftlin zu stulgang. Biblus,ein bintz. Bupleurus,ein kraut. Byssus,köst-cher leinwaht. Cheronesus vel chersonesus,ein halbinsel. Chrysolitus,ein goldfarbig edelgestein. Crystallus,ein Crystallstein. Diphthongus,ein zwenfal-tiger thon. Dialectus,ein eigenschafft zu sprechē. Epirus,ein land das kein Insel ist. Exodus,ein außgang. Eremus,ein wüste. Ficus,ein feigen. Hyssopus,ὕσσωπος. Humus,das Erdtreich Methodus,ein fürtzer weg. Nardus,spica in der Apotek. Papyrus,ein Egyptisch bäumlin darauß man schreibblätter machte. Periodus,ein umbhang. Synodus,ein versamlung. Vannus,ein wann. Et gemmarum & fruticum nomina plæraq;. Neutra sunt,vulgus, dz gemeine volck. Pelagus, die tieffe des Meers. Virus,ein starcker geruch/gifft. Interdum vulgus in masculino genere reperitur. Communia sunt, Barbitus,ein grosse Leire oder Laute. Camelus,ein Camelthier? Carbasus, subtil leinwath/ darauß man schiff sägel macht. Colus,ein rückel / ein spinwocf. Cythisus,grosser Klee. Grossus, ein unzeitige feige. Pampinus,ein weinrebē blatt. Paradisus,ein lustgarten. Phaselus, ein lang schiff. A nominativo in eus,Accusativus definit in a: ut, Orpheus,Orphea.

head.i: Nomina in us quomodo habent in Vocativo?

main_text.p: Nomina Appellativa vel Propria secūdæ declinationis in us,habēt in Vocativo e: ut,Dominus,domine. Tabellarius,tabellarie. Fluvius,fluvie,& fluvius per Antiptosin. Sic Agnus, Chorus populus e & us habere creduntur.Tria appellativa definūt in i: ut,Filius, fili, ein sohn. Meus,mi,mein. Genius, genii,ein Gott oder Engel der natur. Deus, & Lucus,ein geweihter wald/Vocativo manent.At Oedipus,ōOedipu. Propria in ius vel jus abjiciunt in Vocativo us,

page.notes: The first line starts with a Fraktur "und" and a Fraktur "klein" (the k is hard to read, so "klein" is taken from context). Several German words are in black letter and are marked with <bl>; the marking is my reading and may be wrong for some words. "stulgang" and "Methodus" are read with some doubt. The Greek "ὕσσωπος" after Hyssopus is partly illegible in the scan. "Vannus,ein wann" is copied as printed; the word may be a misprint for "mann". "Crystallstein" and "zwenfal-" are printed this way. The heading "Nomina in us quomodo habent in Vocativo?" is in italics; I took it as a level-2 heading.
